title: Separate annual responses limit a 121.54-day Kapteyn wave test to 15 percent Gaussian power in 248 nights
abstract: We test whether public HIRES data resolve the ambiguity between a reported 121.54-day Kapteyn signal and a 121.75-day annual harmonic. We use 217 HARPS nights and 31 HIRES nights. With separate annual waves in three HARPS states and HIRES, group means and trends, and 1.5 m/s added night noise, a 2.25 m/s circular wave has an exact Gaussian upper power bound of 0.1334 to 0.1470 across phases at size 0.05. A common annual wave across all instruments gives bounds of 0.6515 to 0.7473. Thus independent spectra do not resolve this ambiguity under flexible annual responses and the stated covariance. We do not measure an annual error, reject planets, or report a new signal. The calculation uses observation times and errors, not measured velocities. Code, aggregate evidence, proof, validation, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included. External observation records are excluded.
